subject: Clarify standby observability & RPO commitments for multi-region failover
body:
Message 1/4
From: Paul Hughes <paul.hughes@brightbank.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: ops@brightbank.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Clarify standby observability and RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the call earlier. As BrightBank prepares its production cutover to Redwood in eu-west and eu-central, our security and SRE teams need clearer contract language on two items before we sign the final order form:

1) RPO during an automated cross-region switchover — specifically how you define the window (seconds/minutes) for cache/KV sync and whether partial session state is included.
2) Observability coverage during failover — which metrics and traces Redwood will retain and for how long during and immediately after a switchover, and what we can query in real time (especially per-request latency buckets and KV cache hit/miss rates).

We attached a simple spreadsheet with the fields we expect you to fill in (sales asked us to include it). Please treat this as a gating item.

Can you confirm a target RPO number and the expected observability retention/visibility during the 30-minute window after switchover? If you need internal folks from our infra team on a follow-up, loop them in (ops@brightbank.com).

Best,
Paul Hughes
Head of Site Reliability
BrightBank

Attachment: BrightBank_SLA_RTO_RPO_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

----

Message 2/4
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Paul Hughes <paul.hughes@brightbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify standby observability and RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Paul —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the spreadsheet. We can absolutely provide explicit RTO/RPO language; a couple of clarifying points so our legal and infra teams align:

- Are you asking for an absolute RPO cap (e.g., \"RPO <= 2 minutes for session tokens and user-visible state\") or a probabilistic commitment tied to the warm-standby activation window and sequence-length distribution?
- For observability, do you require real-time access to per-request traces for 30 minutes post-switchover, or is an on-demand query/export (within 4 hours) acceptable for compliance audits?

I'm looping in Karthik (serving/infrastructure) for technical guarantees and Logan (product ops) for runbook/visibility commitments. I'll draft proposed clause language after they confirm the operational limits.

Next steps: Karthik, can you review the attached BrightBank worksheet and propose fill-ins for RTO/RPO + observability retention/real-time windows? Logan, if we have a DR runbook link we can share, please include it in the draft.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

----

Message 3/4
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, Paul Hughes <paul.hughes@brightbank.com>
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 13:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify standby observability and RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Paul, Jasmine, Logan —

Technical summary and a proposed redline for the spreadsheet (high level):

- RPO definition: For BrightBank's workload (short-lived sessions + transactional tokens), our warm-standby replication uses continuous KV shadowing plus async object persistence. In practice we can guarantee RPO <= 90s for primary key-value state that is written through our write-through cache. For append-only logs and large objects we recommend an RPO of 5 minutes due to background compaction/replication windows.

- RTO (activation to serving): Our typical warm->hot switch for a pre-warmed standby region is 60–180 seconds depending on concurrent activation requests and model KV warming needs. We define RTO as the time from failover trigger to first successful production response from the secondary region.

- Observability during the 30-minute window: we retain high-resolution request traces and per-route latency histograms for 72 hours in our primary observability cluster. For the switchover window we can provide:
  * Real-time metrics: per-route 99/95/50 latency buckets, per-instance CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss rates exposed to the BrightBank dashboard for 30 minutes post-switchover.
  * Traces: full traces retained and queryable; we can provide a read-only link to the trace viewer within 15 minutes after activation.
  * Logs: request and system logs are available via our audit service; for compliance exports we can deliver an on-demand export within 4 hours.

Proposed SLA clause language (draft):
\"Redwood will maintain an RPO not exceeding ninety (90) seconds for primary key-value session state during an automated or manual cross-region switchover for BrightBank production traffic, subject to the pre-warmed standby configuration detailed in Appendix A. For non-primary append-only artifacts, RPO shall not exceed five (5) minutes. Redwood's activation time (RTO) for pre-warmed standby regions is targeted at sixty (60) to one hundred eighty (180) seconds measured from the failover trigger to the first successful production response.

During the thirty (30) minute post-switchover window, Redwood will expose real-time per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), per-instance GPU/CPU utilization, and KV cache hit/miss metrics via a BrightBank read-only dashboard. Full request traces will be available for query within fifteen (15) minutes of activation and retained for a minimum of seventy-two (72) hours. Logs and audit exports required for regulatory review will be provided on demand within four (4) hours.\"

Attachments: I filled the key fields in the spreadsheet and flagged two items that need legal review:
  - \"subject to the pre-warmed standby configuration\" — this requires BrightBank to opt into the Dedicated pre-warmed pool and maintain the agreed warm capacity (we'll note the required commit in Appendix A).
  - Liability carveouts during widespread region-level network partitions — legal will need to weigh in on language for force majeure / partial availability.

If that aligns, Jasmine / Logan — please circulate to BrightBank and request confirmation; we can iterate on the exact RPO numbers if they pick a different standby profile (cold, warm, or hot).

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-standby-observability-snaps.zip (7 screenshots, 2.1MB)

Message 4/4
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Paul Hughes <paul.hughes@brightbank.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:36:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify standby observability and RPO commitments for multi-region failover

Paul —

Thanks for raising this. The draft language from Karthik is aligned with what Legal and Compliance expect; two operational notes before we finalize the contract:

1) Appendix A (standby profile) will enumerate the warm capacity you need to maintain to receive the 90s RPO and 60–180s RTO. If BrightBank selects a lower-cost cold standby we should reflect longer RPO/RTO in the order form.

2) Observability read-only access requires an onboarding step (SAML group + RBAC) so we will open a short onboarding ticket after contract signature. We'll include a runbook link for the failover play and the on-call rotation for the first 72 hours.

I've populated the BrightBank worksheet with the RPO/RTO numbers and attached the runbook link for your SREs: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/dr/runbooks/brightbank-dr-runbook-v2.pdf

Next steps: Jasmine — please send the updated spreadsheet back to Paul and ask BrightBank to confirm their standby profile (warm vs cold vs hot). Once BrightBank confirms, Legal will prepare a concise order-form addendum and Appendix A.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Compliance and Security
Redwood Inference
